facts.label: Pedir em um food truck
facts.sub: Peça com número + plural + please: Three tacos, please. Escolha o recheio com chicken, beef or fish. Peça menos pimenta com Not too spicy e pergunte How long is the wait?

facts.label: Food trucks
facts.sub: Em cidades grandes dos EUA, food trucks vendem almoço em ruas e parques. Cada um tem um tipo de comida e uma lousa com o cardápio e os preços.

facts.label: Tacos
facts.sub: Tacos são muito populares, principalmente no sul do país. Você escolhe o recheio, como frango, carne ou peixe, e a quantidade, e eles vêm com cebola e coentro.

pages.title: Three tacos · 1/3
paragraphs: It is lunch time on a busy street in Miami. A bright yellow food truck stands near the park. The air smells like grilled meat and fresh lime. Gus stands in the line with a hungry smile. Eli, the cook, works fast behind the window. When Gus reaches the window, Eli says hello.
“Hi! What would you like?” says Eli. “Three tacos, please.” says Gus. “What kind? Chicken, beef or fish?” says Eli.

pages.title: Three tacos · 3/3
paragraphs: “Here you go. How long is the wait, and can I sit at that table?” says Gus. “Five minutes. Sure, take a seat!” says Eli. Eli cooks the tacos on a hot grill. He adds onions, cilantro and a little sauce. Gus pays and takes the paper tray. He sits at a small table under a tree. The tacos are hot, fresh and delicious. A food truck makes a quick and tasty lunch.

pages.what: Em chicken, o “ch” é “tch” e termina com “en” fraco. Em spicy, o “sp” junto é suave, sem “i” antes.
